newsitem.title: ITALY: NIS maintains AA+ rating for Italy long-term debt.
newsitem.headline: NIS maintains AA+ rating for Italy long-term debt.

text.p: Japanese rating agency Nippon Investors Service Inc (NIS) said it had maintained a rating of double A plus on long-term debt for the Republic of Italy in its annual review.
In a statement received in Milan, NIS cited the relative success so far of the government in pushing Italy towards meeting economic conditions to join a single European currency.
Italy's economy was slowing and unemployment remained high at around 12 percent but prices were stabilizing and the lira was appreciating.

Surpluses in both the trade and current account balances have increased, with the ratio of the current account surplus to nominal gross domestic product (GDP) in 1996 "expected to have exceeded three percent as compared to 2.5 percent in the previous year," NIS said.
"Under these circumstances external reserves have continued to grow and the downward trend in net external debt has been maintained," it added.

Summing up, it said the government's stringent fiscal policy coupled with the Bank of Italy's tight monetary policy had brought about a stronger lira and steadier prices and reduced the long-term interest rate differential with Germany.
"On the other hand, the current further tightening of fiscal policy will exert an additional deflationary impact on the economy and place a heavier tax burden on the nation," it said.

"Sustainability of the government's current policy will hence hinge importantly on the success of its efforts in securing the understanding and support of the Italian nation within the environment of the anticipated continuation of slow economic growth," it concluded.
